items.evidence: After deleting, the spec opens the saved draft URL again and expects the not-found message with the draft status hidden (diff lines 66-69). That only passes if the server really deleted the draft. Also, the dashboard only goes to the drafts list when the mutation returns no errors (OrderDraftDetails/index.tsx:175-180).
Criterion 1, the return to the drafts list, is asserted at diff line 63. Criterion 2, the not-found screen on the deleted draft's address, is asserted at diff lines 67-69.
DraftOrderPage had no menu, delete or not-found members. The new ones are added to DraftOrderPage, and the draft is started with the existing create flow.
No fixed waits. delete() waits for the URL to change with waitForURL.
Imports test from fixtures/test.ts, has no parallel() tag and writes no cache files.
Uses test ids show-more-button and cancel-order. The submit button is found inside the dialog. NotFoundPage has no test id, so getByText is the only option.
The only set-up is DraftOrderPage.create, which the checklist allows.
No hard-coded ids. The draft URL is read at runtime, and the channel comes from CHANNEL.name.
Uses the default admin session from the fixture and does not sign in through the UI.
typecheck.txt reports exit 0, and the spec is in e2e/tests/orders/.
All locators and the delete flow are on DraftOrderPage, not in the spec.
The new members are readonly fields built from this.page, and the existing constructor is unchanged.
Has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (diff lines 53, 60).
One test with a test.step for each stage.
The title says what behaviour is checked and includes #e2e.
The header comment at diff lines 45-49 says what the spec covers and why.
All assertions are web-first: toHaveURL, toBeVisible and toBeHidden.
Uses the ORDERS_SCENARIO and CHANNEL constants, with no typed-in literals.
No cleanup code and no unique names.
No custom timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension, and test and expect come only from the fixture.
No any, no casts and no gql calls.
Each comment explains a reason: the 'Cancel order' label, why getByText is used, and why the URL wait proves the deletion succeeded.

structured_output.summary: Submission 93b27983 passes all 23 checklist items (B1–B10, M1–M13). The test starts a draft with DraftOrderPage.create and deletes it through new readonly members and a delete() method on DraftOrderPage. It then reopens the draft's saved URL and expects the not-found screen, which shows the server actually deleted the draft. The type check passes.
